result.title: Preface
result.summary: The November 2021 ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 includes an overview, glossary, cover sheet, questionnaire, and appendices requesting documents and providing templates for team members, references, third parties and technology tools, funds, portfolio investments, GP-led secondaries/continuation funds, and credit facilities. The document lists ILPA’s Washington, D.C. address, phone, and feedback email. Its disclaimer advises parties to respect confidentiality under applicable laws and explains that the DDQ reflects contributors’ views of fund-diligence best practices, but is not a substitute for each limited partner’s judgment about needed information. It also does not guarantee that general partners’ responses will contain all desirable information or everything needed to monitor investments.

result.title: Overview
result.summary: Growing LP focus on alignment, governance and transparency has driven lengthy, customized DDQs that impose administrative burdens despite overlap, while limited peer-sharing leaves some LPs unaware of diligence norms. ILPA developed a standardized DDQ with input from industry participants to reduce redundant work and redirect effort toward transparency and analysis. It is voluntary, does not meet every LP’s needs, and allows justified variation and LP- or GP-specific questions. Its 20 topics span firm and fund information, people and succession, strategy and processes, co-investments and secondaries, facilities, alignment, terms, governance and compliance, performance, accounting, reporting, legal, technology and security, ESG, and diversity, equity and inclusion. Connected yes/no and open-ended questions guide diligence and further GP engagement; an appendix lists requested documents and data. Supporting materials include a changes summary, user guide and glossary, and PRI guidance for ESG. ILPA plans more regular reviews as practices evolve and welcomes feedback by email. The terminology section defines leadership, senior and other professionals, investment professionals, team members, principals, employees, C-suite, C-suite minus one, and portfolio-company senior management.

result.title: Glossary
result.summary: The glossary defines firm and investment leadership (senior leaders responsible for overall firm oversight and final deal decisions, often sharing in carried interest and/or management-company profits); operations and administration leadership (leaders of finance, marketing, investor relations, legal, HR and administrative functions, with possible investment input and carried interest); and firm leadership as both groups together. Senior investment professionals make investment decisions without being firm leaders and may include operating partners. Other investment professionals, such as principals, vice presidents, associates and analysts, support deal sourcing through management and may share in carried interest or profits. Other operations and administration professionals cover operating, communications, finance, legal and administrative roles. It also defines investment staff as the three investment levels, fund staff as all five levels working directly on the fund, current leadership/investment professionals as self-identified in Appendix B1, all firm employees regardless of role or focus, CEO and direct senior-executive reports, employees reporting directly to C-suite management, and portfolio-company C-suite and C-suite-minus-one.

result.title: Cover Sheet
result.summary: A cover sheet collecting firm details (name, address, phone, supervising regulators and registration numbers, and contact person details) and fund details (investment adviser/manager, GP and fund legal names, manager regulators and registration numbers). It records fund size and reporting currency; management fees; target, minimum and maximum amounts; first-close amount, amounts raised and number of closings; investment, follow-on and extension periods; investment, strategic, geographic and industry focus; ESG/impact/sustainable strategy; completion date and fund term; and fund-specific dates and term periods. It also captures miscellaneous terms, hurdle rate, carried interest, carry catch-up and escrow, and GP commitment.

result.title: Questionnaire
result.summary: The questionnaire examines the firm’s history, ownership, structure, leadership, staffing, culture, succession, outside activities, growth plans, finances, and governance, risk and compliance policies. It asks about fund structure, fundraising, investors, terms, fees, meetings, borrowing, expenses, leadership changes, team compensation and commitments, and investment strategy, markets, sourcing, diligence, allocations, co-investments, continuation funds, portfolio management, value creation, exits and track record. It covers accounting, valuation, tax, administration, audit, reporting, investor relations, legal matters, cybersecurity, technology, service providers and controls. It also addresses ESG policies and governance, ESG integration throughout investment and portfolio-company lifecycles, climate commitments and emissions, incident management, reporting, internal firm practices and other ESG topics. Diversity, equity and inclusion questions cover metrics, policies, hiring, retention, pay, accountability, investment practices, portfolio-company diversity and private-market initiatives. Respondents are often asked for examples, documents, policies, plans and disclosures.
